name: FESPACO
funding: About 1.3-1.5bn FCFA executed in 2025 (~US$2.3M), nearly 80% from the Burkina state; EU 195M FCFA, plus the UN, OIF, LONAB lottery and telecoms.

name: Musée National du Burkina Faso
funding: State museum (EPSCT) with 30,000+ visits Jan-Oct 2024, funded by the culture ministry plus Ouagadougou commune, Agence Faso Mɛbo and unnamed company donors.

name: Sa Sa Art Projects
funding: Artist-run. Funding found: an online artist auction (2022), documenta fifteen money for a community studio, and a Rei Foundation partnership from 2018 to 2024. No funder list is published.

name: Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum
funding: Run by Cambodia's Ministry of Culture and Fine Arts, which lists it among its institutions. Foreign adults pay $5 and Cambodians enter free, the museum states.

name: Angkor Panorama Museum
funding: Mansudae built it with North Korean money, reported at US$24 million, and co-ran it with Cambodia's APSARA Authority. Its director said in 2016 Mansudae would take ten years' profit.

name: Bandjoun Station
funding: Small artist-run centre opened 2013, paid for by Barthélémy Toguo, his coffee plantations and the Amis de Bandjoun Station association.

name: Musée National du Cameroun
funding: State museum under the Ministry of Arts and Culture; €1M modernisation from AFD via debt-swap C2D (2019-24), Phase 2 2025-27, run by Expertise France.

name: Contemporary Calgary
funding: Individual Leadership Circle and lifetime donors. LOOK gala presented by Mawer (2025), Rogers (2023) and National Bank (2020 to 2022); Holt Renfrew sponsors the dinner.

name: Confederation Centre of the Arts
funding: C$20.7M revenue 2023-24 (C$15.1M public grants incl. C$8.6M capital), C$402k sponsorship; Sobey foundations, Cavendish Farms, CN, TD, BMO, RBC, Pepsico, Maritime Electric.

name: Art Gallery of Hamilton
funding: C$7.8M revenue (2024). Funders: Canada Council, Ontario Arts Council, City of Hamilton, incite Foundation, BMO, TD, RBC, LiUNA, Peller Estates, CHCH.

name: Musée d'art de Joliette
funding: Quebec ministries, Canada Council and Ville de Joliette. Énergir, Power Corporation, Fondation Hydro-Québec, Caisse Desjardins and the Lassonde and DeSève foundations are among its lead partners (2025 annual report).
